verdicts.evidence: lines 488-492: every .copy button gets a click listener; lines 465-486 copy the code text via clipboard API with execCommand fallback. The 15 Copy buttons are the only buttons; links at 257-266 and 419-421 are real hrefs.
lines 248-426: static documentation prose and commands; no records, counts, metrics or charts are displayed.
One-screen page with no stepped inputs; the only dependency (snapshot id for restore) is explained in place at lines 363 and 368.
No inputs, forms or free text anywhere in the file; nothing to lose on reload.
No preselected values, dialogs or default buttons; only Copy buttons (line 287 and similar).
The frequent task is copying a command; each command block has its own Copy button in place (e.g. lines 285-289, 348-352), one click, no other screen or dialog.

Sections at 272-423 map one to one to the brief notes. Added crontab -e (381), env export commands (326-334) and the sudo command (410) carry out steps the brief names. The table of contents (254-268) is navigation for the same content.
lines 171-185: all Copy buttons share one outlined secondary style (surface background, accent text); no button is filled as primary.
No control on the page deletes or overwrites anything; the buttons only copy text.
No disabled controls. Copy buttons are hidden in markup (line 287) and revealed by script (line 490), so without script they are absent, not greyed out.
No title attributes, tooltips or hover cards in the markup or script.
lines 245-423: all visible text is about harbour, its commands and its problems; nothing mentions the build, framework, brief or mock data.

line 315: the single callout (passphrase cannot be recovered) sits directly above the harbour init command (317) where the passphrase is chosen and tells the reader to store it. No other callouts or banners.

line 251: 'This page takes you from installing it to a first backup, a restore and a nightly schedule.' narrates the page itself, the same pattern as 'This page lets you', and duplicates the contents list at 255-267.

Section headings have no subtitles restating them (273, 282, 313, 347, 357, 367, 378). Minor repetition only: line 277 'No other software. harbour has no dependencies.'; passphrase facts at 315 and 405 serve different sections.
lines 250-251, 273-423: headings are task names ('Install harbour', 'Restore files'); no greeting, slogan, superlative or exclamation mark; claims are concrete (60 MB, 02:00, glibc 2.31).

lines 287, 294 and similar: label 'Copy', a specific verb; each button sits inside the box of the one command it copies and carries aria-describedby pointing at that code, so the object is unambiguous. Changes to 'Copied' (471).

'repository' and 'snapshot' are defined in plain words where introduced (314, 363); error strings at 396-407 are the literal messages the user sees in the terminal; no field names or enum values as labels.

line 483: the only error the page can raise reads 'Could not copy. The command is selected, so you can copy it by hand.' It states what happened and the next step, with no codes; line 481 selects the text for the user.
line 483 error text and line 315 warning are neutral statements; no 'invalid', 'failed', 'oops', exclamation marks or capitals in visible text ('failed' appears only as a class name).
No list, table, feed or search that can have zero items; all content is fixed markup.
No filters, search or loaded data; no view can be empty.
Fully static page; script (428-494) makes no network requests.
The only action is a clipboard write (447-455), which resolves well under a second.
No asynchronous data, no loading or empty states.
Only fixed text is displayed; no variable-length data values. Long commands wrap via pre-wrap and overflow-wrap (164-170).
The page holds no edits.
No form fields in the file.
No form fields in the file.
No form and no validation.
No form that can reject input.
No form that can be rejected.
No form that can reject input.
No form or submit button on the page.
No form with a server effect.
line 185: .copy:active gives an immediate pressed state; lines 469-473 change the label to 'Copied' as soon as the clipboard promise resolves.
lines 470-478: success shows 'Copied' on the button for 2 seconds; lines 479-484: failure selects the command and shows a visible message under it.
lines 471-473: the only success signal is the button label 'Copied' (plus a visually hidden status line, 197-204); a clipboard write is not otherwise visible on screen.
lines 479-484: the failure note is set with no timer, so it stays in place under the command until the next copy attempt; only the action-free 'Copied' label reverts on a 2 second timer (474-478).
No action removes, archives, moves or changes anything.
No irreversible action in the interface itself.
No confirmation dialogs.
No optimistic updates or background requests.
No modal dialogs.
No modal dialogs.
lines 249-252: h1 and lead come first at the largest type size (100); the contents list is small muted text (132-146), in a side column at 60rem and up (211-229); instructions follow directly.
lines 244-252: a one-line header, then h1 and a two-sentence lead sized to content (no min-height or viewport units); no hero, greeting or intro panel before the instructions.
No summary numbers, stat cards or charts.
No filtering, search or sorting.
All interactive elements are native a and button type=button elements (257-266, 287 etc, 419-421) with click handlers that fire on Enter and Space; focus-visible outline at line 63; no focus trap.
line 315: the warning has a coloured left border (206-209) plus bold text stating it; line 483: the error is danger-coloured (195) but is a full sentence. No colour-only signals.

line 288 and each block: an empty p.copy-note with role=status exists in the markup on load and is filled at 473 and 483. The copy failure is announced through role=status, not role=alert, but it is in a pre-existing live region.
Nothing expands or collapses; no accordions, menus or tabs.

line 94: single column below 60rem; 164-170 commands wrap inside their box; 155-158 Copy button stays in an auto column; 234-236 gutters drop to 1rem at 30rem; contents list is plain block links (147-151). Nothing is cut off at 375px.
Single page with no site navigation: the header (245) has no links, and the only nav is an in-page contents list of anchors (254-268).
One view with no tabs, filters, pagination or selection state. Section anchors (257-266) do put the hash in the URL against heading ids.
Single-view page; no script touches history.

lines 416-423: the page ends with links to the three next pages (/docs/excludes, /docs/retention, /docs/check); contents links at 257-266. The header 'harbour Documentation' (245) is not a link to a docs home.
No dialogs or overlays.
No stepped flow UI; all instructions are on one page.

lines 173-174: Copy button min-width 4.75rem and min-height 2.75rem (44px) below 60rem; lines 147-150: contents links are block with 0.75rem vertical padding around a 20px line, about 44px. The 2.25rem override (232) applies only at 60rem and up.

lines 219-229: the contents list is sticky only at 60rem and up, in its own 14rem grid column beside the content, with max-height calc(100vh - 3rem) and its own scroll; it covers no content. Nothing is fixed or sticky at phone widths.

lines 250-251: 'Getting started with harbour' then 'harbour makes encrypted, de-duplicated backups of folders to a local disk or to any S3-compatible storage.' A reader can say what it is and that it is for someone backing up folders.
A documentation article with no single main action for the visitor; no call-to-action button.
No img, svg, video or background imagery in the file.
No testimonials, customer names, usage figures, ratings or prices. Technical figures (version 2.4, 60 MB, OS versions at 245, 275-276) match the brief.
No pricing section.
No images or video.
No announcement strip; the header at 244-246 is a plain site title line.
All 15 command blocks (286-411) have a button labelled 'Copy' wired at 488-492 that copies the code element's text (469) and changes to 'Copied' (471), with a fallback message on failure (483).

lines 16-18: one accent, hue 245, used for links (64), Copy button text (179) and focus outlines (63). Warning (19) and danger (20) are status colours used only on the passphrase callout border and the copy error. Everything else is neutral.
